items.summary: OpenAI's third-quarter revenue reached US$10 billion (S$12.8 billion), a nearly 50% rise from the prior quarter, driven by strong demand for its latest AI software, according to a person familiar with the matter who spoke on condition of anonymity because the figures are not public. The details were shared with investors during a Nov. 10 call; OpenAI declined to comment.
items.title: OpenAI Q3 Revenue Surges Nearly 50% Past $10 Billion

items.summary: Meta introduces Triton Low-Level Extensions (TLX), a hardware-native compiler extension that adds explicit warp-group and cluster-level orchestration to the Triton programming model, letting ML engineers adopt modern NVIDIA Hopper and Blackwell features without leaving Python. The authors report using it in production across Meta’s recommendation systems and large-scale LLM pretraining. In GEM training they cite O(10^24) total training flops with 20-25% end-to-end MFU, near-optimal performance on a generalized dot-product attention kernel (up to 2x forward speedup), a 4x speedup from an in-kernel broadcast optimization on the H100, and up to two-thirds reduction in net latency for co-designed FlashAttention kernels. TLX is positioned as occupying the middle ground between CUDA’s control and Triton’s productivity.
items.title: Meta Ships TLX Compiler for Production GPU Workloads

items.summary: Amazon is introducing an AI-powered Ring security drone and robot for home or office patrols, per a November 10 announcement. The Ring Rover Cam may reach customers by end of 2026; the Ring Drone Cam in early 2027. Both use an AI Pilot system with vision models and sensors to map spaces and plan routes. Flying devices could add privacy risks beyond existing fixed-camera concerns, though Amazon notes they follow set schedules for Protect subscribers.
items.title: Amazon Launches AI Security Drone and Robot

items.summary: New research from security firm Claroc shows the vibe-coding agent Grok Build, made by SpaceXSI (the now-merged SpaceX and xAI), leaks proprietary business information and sensitive secrets from thousands of users. Links let people share apps; a developer design flaw lets anyone enumerate live projects and view all associated data, including internal plans, medical results and employee IDs—some even from SpaceXSI's own 24 apps.
items.title: SpaceXSI Grok Build Agent Leaks Confidential User Data

items.summary: A survey commissioned by Syfe and conducted by YouGov among Singaporean adults found that major life expenses, such as buying a first home or raising children, slow investing momentum even though many want to invest more. About 65% of those who saw their first job as their biggest financial milestone invested more later, versus 49% in Hong Kong and 42% in Australia. Confidence falls sharply with age: 40% of Singaporeans aged 18 to 24 are highly confident about investing, but only 12% among those above 55. The survey suggests the challenge is helping people feel informed enough to stay invested through life's stages.
items.title: Singaporeans Want More Investing But Life Costs Hold Them Back

items.summary: OpenAI has acquired an AI travel agent called Odessia, according to its founder Francis Davidson, who now works for the lab on travel's future. Terms were not disclosed and this looks like an acqui-hire; OpenAI confirmed the hire but announced no new travel products or plans.
items.title: OpenAI Acquires AI Travel Startup Odessia

items.summary: In its S-1 filing for an anticipated $1.4 trillion valuation, Anthropic disclosed that each of its seven co-founders plans to sell 3,378,378 shares. At the midrange price of $74 per share, each founder would take in just shy of $250 million; at the low end ($70), over $236 million, and at the high end ($78), under $264 million.
items.title: Anthropic Founders Set To Cash Out In IPO

items.summary: Experts are concerned that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's calls to loosen chip export restrictions on China may have been influenced by an alleged affair with Alice Huang, a Singapore-based Megaspeed customer leader suspected of Chinese government ties. The Trump administration reportedly knew about the relationship for some time but never warned Huang.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Faces Alleged Spy Scandal Over China Chip Ties

items.summary: ZDNET reports that Apple plans to charge users a one-time $50 fee, rather than a subscription, to access server-based AI capacity in some apps starting with Creator Studio. The move lets the company offset AI costs as usage packs roll out through app updates.
items.title: Apple May Charge a One-Time $50 Fee for AI Tools in Creator Studio Apps

items.summary: Microsoft released the Windows 10 KB5131096 extended security update, bundling this month's November 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes with additional bug fixes. The update addresses 1,235 vulnerabilities across Microsoft's products, including one actively exploited Outlook zero-day flaw claim-693-903 . It also resolves known issues affecting USB Audio Class 1.0 devices introduced by the September 2026 Windows security updates claim-2530-2678 , and includes a daylight saving time adjustment for Cuba. Running Enterprise LTSC users can install it via Settings > Windows Update, after which systems move to build 19045.7846 or 19044.7846 date-107-111 .
items.title: Microsoft ships Windows 10 KB5131096 security update

items.summary: A threat actor used compromised Qubole IAM credentials to access and exfiltrate data from multiple customers' AWS environments between October 14 and 26. Researchers at Wiz, with Sentra's information and Mandiant involvement, found the attacker assumed unused roles across accounts trusting Qubole's account, then pulled secrets and downloaded all accessible S3 buckets opportunistically. Sentra confirmed dozens of victims and millions of files stolen from one customer alone.
items.title: Qubole AWS Trust Breach Exposed Multiple Cloud Customers

items.summary: Microsoft researchers describe “Lazarus,” a backdoor technique that reprograms dormant neurons in an LLM so an otherwise normal agent executes malicious commands when a hidden trigger appears. The researcher who first discovered the threat reports that weight-reprogramming fewer than 10 dormant neurons is enough to backdoor an agent and requires no training, with one reprogrammed neuron able to inject one token into the residual stream. A triggered model can pass standard evaluations while downloading and running attacker code using whatever access it has. Microsoft Foundry mitigates this by verifying provenance, tying models to trusted publishers, scanning environments, and developing weight scanning, red-teaming tools, and cryptographic signing.
items.title: Microsoft Researchers Detail Lazarus AI Backdoor Technique

items.summary: In a ForeCast episode of Forethought's interview podcast, Avi Parrack and Tom Davidson discuss how SpaceX could reach roughly 99% of global launch capacity once Starship flies. They cover Golden Dome interceptors, whether the US might use its lead to exclude rivals from space, possible countermeasures such as jamming or strikes on launch sites, risks to nuclear deterrence, and first-mover advantages in industrialising the solar system.
items.title: Forethought podcast on US space and launch dominance

items.summary: Databricks announced that Unity Catalog metric views are now available through Publish to Power BI, giving organizations a single governed semantic layer shared across reports and AI applications. Previously, teams maintained separate metrics in Databricks and thousands of Power BI workspaces with their own Semantic Models, causing definitions to drift. The feature lets each metric view become a table in the model, keeping one definition as source of truth while joins run in Databricks. A marketing example shows campaign performance published automatically via Lakeflow Jobs or on demand. Publish to Power BI is currently available in Private Preview.
items.title: Databricks Brings Unity Catalog Metric Views to Power BI

items.summary: Agent Substrate is an open-source, security-hardened runtime donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation that multiplexes many agent sessions over a small pool of worker Pods. The project claims 10x higher density than standard containers by checkpointing idle sessions and restoring them onto free workers without cold starts. NVIDIA contributes upstream because agentic infrastructure is fragmenting into proprietary runtimes. It works alongside KAI Scheduler for placement, which places ordinary Kubernetes Pods today, and with NVIDIA Dynamo to coordinate CPU-side tool execution with GPU inference across the model-call loop. The integration exposes inference signals so Agent Substrate can keep or suspend actors based on cache readiness and queue pressure. Parts of the Dynamo agent integration are experimental as of 2026.
items.title: NVIDIA Donates Agent Substrate Runtime and Pairs It With Dynamo for Agentic Workloads

items.summary: Yasodara Cordova argues Brazil's AI strategy overemphasizes frontier models and data centers, ignoring edge computing. The country announced 2.3 billion reais ($444.2 million) for supercomputing projects [quantity-641-658][quantity-660-674]. A July 2026 Getulio Vargas Foundation study estimated that only about 4% of a model's jobs become permanent roles, versus 85% tied to construction [date-5581-5585][entity-5586-5617][quantity-5678-5681][quantity-5745-5747]. Meanwhile, the federal Nova Indústria Brasil policy set aside 300 billion reais through 2026 [date-6324-6328][entity-6245-6272][quantity-6347-6364]. Cordova contends edge AI better suits Brazil's industrial needs and existing repair workforce, though the government currently favors centralized infrastructure.
items.title: Brazil's AI Plan Should Embrace Edge Computing Over Data Centers

items.summary: The author argues walking ability is a better, cost-free indicator of health than grip strength. Citing a 2015 Lancet study of 139,691 people, every 5kg weaker grip linked to 16% higher all-cause mortality. Local Timed Up and Go averages (9.8 seconds) fall below the commonly cited Western figure (12.3), so foreign thresholds may miss at-risk older adults; local risk rises past about 10.2 seconds, with disability odds roughly doubling or tripling beyond about 9.45 seconds.
items.title: Walking ability trumps grip strength as a free health marker

items.summary: As ships face renewed mine risk in the Strait of Hormuz, navies are increasingly turning to autonomous robot systems instead of crewed vessels. Former merchant navy officer Steve Cameron notes that captains must weigh war-risk insurance and danger before transit, while naval architect Ian McFarlane calls mines a cheap way of waging naval war. Autonomous robots like Thales's Uncrewed Surface Vehicle use sonar and AI to map the seabed without putting sailors at risk; analyst William Lupton says avoiding captured personnel is central to their appeal. Steve Prest notes that although no mines can be proven absent, such systems reduce risk as part of a broader cognitive architecture.
items.title: Nations Turn to Robot Vessels for Mine Hunting

items.summary: Peter Lewis argues the Labor–creative sector alliance is at a crossroads as Anthony Albanese pursues an AI strategy centred on embedding Australia in model production. The piece notes Anthropic, seeking $1.5tn valuation, has pitched Australian training models. A competing narrative holds that models were trained on scraped material without creator consent. Lewis frames the dispute beyond copyright: automated mimicry of artists' work and concerns across mathematics, education, psychology and humanity itself. He flags rising energy, water and inflation pressures from datacentre scale-out. Creatives are described as emotional and principled, angered by a PM promise in his July AI speech. They expect control over their work and meaningful reparation. Lewis calls for clear labelling, promotion of human work and shared value beyond intellectual property, likening it to Bob Hawke's union agreement.
items.title: Albanese faces creative backlash over AI and copyright

items.summary: The Tech Life programme previews its content, opening with an investigation into how everyday connected devices face a wave of cyber-attacks on commercial fridges. It also features listener experiences as a moderator for a pornography service, the effect of US Midterm elections on global tech, and another listener's technical time troubles. Presenter Chris Vallance produced it with Imran Rahman-Jones.
items.title: Tech Life episode covers cyberattacks and tech topics

items.summary: Unplugged Performance publicly offered on Tuesday to take the Cybertruck line off Tesla’s hands, funded by a consortium of investors. The pitch came four days after Elon Musk said Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at Giga Texas around mid-2027, with sales running at roughly 12% of the 250,000 units a year Tesla planned for. UP says it supports prioritizing Cybercab and would run the truck “at no cost to Tesla’s floor space, headcount, or focus,” while collecting a license fee plus FSD and Robotaxi revenue. The post passed 240,000 views within hours; neither Musk nor Tesla had responded at writing. Electrek notes demand is the real problem: Q3 saw 8,295 Other Models delivered, about 7,000 to 8,000 of which were Cybertrucks — a pace of roughly 30,000 trucks a year — even though Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet and the line runs at about a quarter of its 125,000-unit capacity.
items.title: Tesla Tuner Offers to Take Over Cybertruck Production

items.summary: Border communities in Texas voted overwhelmingly for Democratic candidates last Tuesday, with every U.S.-Mexico border House seat expected to flip by January and Democrats sweeping all 18 statewide races. Despite these gains, the Trump administration retains funding—$46.5 billion appropriated through the One Big Beautiful Bill Act—and statutory authority under a 2005 Real ID waiver to continue wall construction in ecologically sensitive areas like Big Bend. Advocates urge Democrats to use their new congressional and state majorities to investigate contracts, block park access, and restrict appropriations. A Supreme Court ruling Monday overturned an injunction that had paused work there.
items.title: Texas Democrats Target Border Wall After Midterm Gains

items.summary: An NPR interview explores concerns over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's expanding influence at his company and across the American tech industry, framed by a scandal that may carry wide-ranging implications for how technology firms are led.
items.title: Nvidia scandal could reshape tech leadership

items.summary: According to the Wall Street Journal, OpenAI's third-quarter revenue rose about 50 per cent to $10 billion while operating losses widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion. The company told investors its adjusted operating margin improved to -109 per cent from -150 per cent in the prior quarter, though it did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. The disclosure arrives as rival Anthropic prepares an IPO that could value it at about $1.4 trillion.
items.title: OpenAI Posts Steep Losses as Revenue Hits $10 Billion in Third Quarter

items.summary: According to a Bloomberg report, Anthropic PBC is seeking about $1.4 trillion valuation in an initial public offering that could make it the first frontier AI laboratory to go public. The company and some backers aim to raise as much as $90.4 billion through the IPO and private placement.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for $1.4 Trillion Valuation in Record IPO

items.summary: The US Securities and Exchange Commission asked a Manhattan federal judge to close the $40 million Fair Fund created after Elon Musk settled its 2018 securities fraud case. A claims administrator distributed $41.53 million, including interest, to 3,350 eligible claimants who received 51.7 per cent of approved claims because losses exceeded the fund's size; another 3,046 claims were rejected. The SEC said about $449,000 remaining will go to the US Treasury. "Distribution of the Fair Fund is now complete," the SEC said.
items.title: SEC Moves to Close Musk Tesla Fair Fund

items.summary: Joon Kim, a former acting US Attorney for the Southern District of New York, has been tapped to lead an internal probe into whether Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese espionage campaign. The assignment follows Huang’s admission Sunday that he had an extramarital affair with a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia shares have dropped 10% since the disclosure, knocking $500 billion off its market value. Kim will oversee the investigation into whether trade secrets or national security interests were compromised by a committee of independent directors. The company maintains it has no reason to believe either was breached.
items.title: Nvidia Names Former Prosecutor To Probe Huang Espionage Allegations

items.summary: IBM said Tuesday it was discontinuing its sponsorship of US visas and green cards in its largest division, a move the item frames as a win for the Trump administration. The article notes White House proposals including $100,000 filing fees for H-1B visas, which critics call a corporate tax on foreign talent.
items.title: IBM ends visa sponsorship in largest division

items.summary: Anthropic introduced upgraded Claude Feable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 models, claiming its more than 1000 AI agents built an operating-system prototype within eight days. The company says the models answer about 30% faster and found more software weaknesses in testing.
items.title: Anthropic's AI agents build operating system in eight days

items.summary: Research company Circana reports UK toy sales up to October were 17% higher than the same period last year, with growth at a 10-year high. Despite cost-of-living pressures, there is significant growth in toys priced between £5 and £10. Connected toys account for less than 1% of market sales, showing traditional play remains popular.
items.title: Toy sales rise ahead of Christmas as traditional play stays popular

items.summary: NPR poses whether readers should trust new agentic AI systems with their money and data, noting tech companies want such agents to become the primary way people shop. The outlet frames this as an open question about consumer confidence when financial stakes are involved. NPR states it does not offer or accept payment for coverage or interviews, warning that anyone making such requests is not affiliated with the organization.
items.title: NPR Questions Trust in Agentic AI for Money and Data

items.summary: Official data shows China's trade surplus exceeded $US1 trillion in the first 10 months, surpassing last year's record. Exports rose 35.2 per cent to $US412.3 billion and imports grew 41.6 per cent to $US307.1 billion. The boom is driven by AI-related products amid weak domestic demand, as Beijing relies on exports toward its 4.5-5.0 per cent growth target while trade tensions with the US and EU persist.
items.title: China's Trade Surplus Tops $1 Trillion for Second Straight Year

items.summary: Nima Momeni was sentenced to 16 years to life in the murder of Cash App founder Bob Lee, convicted by a jury of second-degree murder. The killing occurred on 4 April 2023 under the Bay Bridge after an alleged feud surfaced during the trial. During sentencing, Lee’s daughter Scout Lee and Momeni’s mother Mahnaz Tayarani spoke to the judge, while Momeni expressed remorse.
items.title: Man Sentenced for Killing Cash App Founder Bob Lee

items.summary: Macquarie Bank will pay a court-imposed civil penalty after admitting it broke the Corporations Act through its welcome rate promotions. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission pursued action over savings conditions that risked short-changing customers amid rising living costs. Macquarie said in court proceedings it failed to provide financial services efficiently, honestly and fairly.
items.title: Macquarie Bank Faces $14m Penalty Over Confusing Savings Promotion

items.summary: The US House voted 211-204 to refer impeachment articles against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to a committee, effectively killing the effort. Introduced by Republican Thomas Massie, who accused Hegseth of waging war on Iran for over 90 days without authorisation, it failed as more than a dozen members were absent. Hegseth dismissed it as sabotage; Trump celebrated the outcome.
items.title: House Rejects Impeachment Bid Against Hegseth

items.summary: The US Department of Justice announced charges against three Iran-backed operatives alleged to have taken part in a series of plots across the US and Europe. The indictment accuses them, most recently, of orchestrating an attack at RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire in September 2026, where seven men were arrested. Iranian officials deny involvement. Kash Patel said the accused supported Iran's IRGC and Kataib Hezbollah in nearly 20 attempted attacks, while a DOJ statement noted that HAYI claimed responsibility for 18 of those attacks across Europe, seven in the UK.
items.title: US Charges Three Iran-Backed Operatives Over UK and European Plots

items.summary: At least 11 National Security Agency and U.S. Cyber Command workers died by suicide over roughly the past year, according to officials and public records, more than previously known. From early June to early July, five such deaths occurred, prompting a so-called suicide cluster designation. White House and congressional staff questioned agency leaders privately, while military commanders adjusted long work hours and expanded mental health support amid surging workloads tied to foreign conflicts.
items.title: Congress Scrutinizes Surge in NSA and Cyber Command Suicides

items.summary: Despite market bets on a de-escalation in the Iran war, new evidence has emerged of strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and energy infrastructure. Crude prices hit two-month lows after U.S. officials downplayed further military action following Trump's conciliatory tone post-November 3 midterms. Yet attacks show little sign of abating: 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the war began, per the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.
items.title: Tankers Burn in Middle East Despite De-escalation Hopes

items.summary: Golf player Minjee Lee is expected to skip the LPGA Tour Championship in Naples from November 19-22, ending her difficult 2026 season. Her world ranking has fallen from third to 24th, described as her equal-lowest standing in 11 years. This would be her first absence from the event since 2014.
items.title: Minjee Lee set to miss Tour Championship after poor season

items.summary: In an interview, Bert Hofman, former World Bank country director for China, Mongolia and Korea, argues that APEC's real value lies not in signing agreements but in providing a forum where major competitors can continue to cooperate. He says the most important outcome of this year's meeting in Shenzhen is trust—trust in trade and in international cooperation.
items.title: Bert Hofman on APEC's Role in Global Cooperation

items.summary: Anthropic and its co-founders are seeking up to $90.4 billion through an IPO and private placement, per a Tuesday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The base offering could raise as much as $64.4 billion, with shares priced between $70 and $78 each. A greenshoe option would lift the total to roughly $100 billion, surpassing SpaceX's prior offerings.
items.title: Anthropic Aims for $90.4 Billion IPO at Record Valuation

items.summary: According to documents viewed by The Wall Street Journal, OpenAI reported an adjusted operating margin improving to -109% from -150%, while its operating losses widened to $10.9 billion from $10.1 billion in the prior quarter. Reuters sought comment; OpenAI did not respond immediately. The disclosure arrives as investors scrutinize AI finances, including Anthropic's potential IPO valued at about $1.4 trillion.
items.title: OpenAI posts steep losses even as quarterly revenue rises to $10 billion

items.summary: IBM said Tuesday it was ending US visa and green card sponsorship for a majority of roles in IBM Consulting, which employs more than 150,000 people. The move comes amid scrutiny of foreign tech hiring by the Trump administration, following last month's suspension of Microsoft, Adobe and several outsourcers from Permanent Labor Certification. A company spokesperson said participation had been declining as skill availability and client needs evolved.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa and Green Card Sponsorship for Most Consulting Roles

items.summary: Nvidia said on Tuesday it hired New York-based Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead a thorough and independent investigation into allegations surrounding chief executive Jensen Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, accused of spying for China. Nvidia's shares fell close to a one-year low, wiping about $500 billion (£375 billion) off its market value since Friday.
items.title: Nvidia Hires Law Firm Over CEO Spy Allegations

items.summary: IBM said it discontinued visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in IBM Consulting, its largest division of over 150,000 workers. Impacted employees may keep working outside the US or leave by year's end. The move follows pressure from the Trump administration on tech firms to hire American staff amid immigration concerns.
items.title: IBM Ends Visa Sponsorship in Largest Unit

items.summary: A California judge found Tesla liable for fraud and negligent misrepresentation in a lawsuit brought by Ambrose Conroy of Rancho Santa Fe, whose never-completed Solar Roof failed to generate electricity. The ruling follows repeated failures by the company to produce documents during discovery, including internal messages describing the project as an experiment. Judge Cynthia Freeland rejected Tesla's request to reconsider the decision on October 27.
items.title: California judge finds Tesla liable for Solar Roof fraud

items.summary: The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau (TGCSB) registered a suo motu case under Section 67B of the IT Act after receiving three alerts routed through NCMEC and I4C. The alerts, generated by Google, concerned suspected online circulation of child sexual abuse material tied to a Google profile. Before registering the case, officials conducted preliminary checks of IP addresses, mobile numbers and email IDs.
items.title: Telangana Cyber Bureau Registers Case Over Google Alerts

items.summary: In an SEC filing Tuesday, Anthropic said it plans to raise up to $64 billion by selling 825 million shares at a debut price estimate of between $70 and $78 per share, implying a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. Earlier estimates had reached as high as $2 trillion amid falling AI stock prices.
items.title: Anthropic Sets $1.4 Trillion Valuation in IPO Filing

items.summary: According to the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology's models, firecracker emissions made up more than 80% of Delhi's pollution load on Monday after Diwali. The city had already faced high pollution from multiple sources before the festival.
items.title: Firecrackers Accounted for Majority of Delhi Pollution After Diwali

items.summary: The VHP accused Sonia Gandhi of 'selective outrage' for mourning the Babri demolition but not other events. Surendra Jain questioned her silence on temple demolitions, Kashmir massacres and Sikh killings in Delhi.
items.title: VHP Accuses Sonia Gandhi of Selective Outrage Over Hindu Tragedies

items.summary: The US dollar index closed near its highest level since October 28, up 0.5% after October consumer prices rose more than expected amid higher food and accommodation costs. Markets now price an 84% chance of a rate hike next month, with better-than-even odds for a January second hike.
items.title: Dollar Steady as Fed Hike Odds Rise on Hot Inflation Data

items.summary: Democratic Senator Chuck Schumer accused President Donald Trump of inaction after being briefed more than a year ago about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, whom US authorities identified as a suspected Chinese spy. Schumer posted on X that "Trump was briefed over A YEAR AGO" and "did nothing about it," while also criticizing the president for taking Huang to Beijing and accepting a $25 million donation from Nvidia. The allegations follow a New York Times report citing Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who reportedly reminded Trump again in May. Trump denied knowing about the relationship during his China visit but later defended Huang as an honorable man. An FBI probe and congressional review are underway.
items.title: Schumer Accuses Trump of Shielding Jensen Huang Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: Finshots explains that Indian companies are increasingly investing overseas, driving net foreign direct investment down from $43.9 billion to $6.7 billion in FY26 while outward flows rose from $18 billion to a record $49 billion over the same period. The outlet offers reasons for this trend—market access, acquiring capabilities and domestic spillovers—and notes that money leaving India can still bring value back through profits and exports. It also flags concerns about profit shifting, rupee pressure and round-tripping, concluding that the real question is whether these investments generate enough economic benefit at home.
items.title: India's Outward FDI Surges as Companies Invest Abroad

items.summary: Sonia Gandhi’s memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love hit the stands on Tuesday, sparking political debates online and on television channels. However, contrary to expectations, the book contains few big revelations, focusing mostly on her life before politics. The period after 2004 is covered only in passing. Amitabh Bachchan's name appears just three times in the book, while his wife Jaya Bachchan is not mentioned at all. Political opponents like Lal Krishna Advani and Amit Shah are absent or briefly discussed. Sonia Gandhi recounts declining to become prime minister before Manmohan Singh, describing how alliance leaders pressured her until she mumbled 'Theek hai.' She also reflects on Indira Gandhi's early terrors in Parliament. The book acknowledges Emergency excesses while shifting some blame onto Sanjay and Maneka Gandhi.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi's memoir offers few surprises

items.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis defended the BJP-led Mahayuti government's decision to draft a Uniform Civil Code, citing constitutional Directive Principles of State Policy. He responded to AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi's claim that the law was unconstitutional and Hindu-imposed. On the NCP merger question, he said neither Sharad Pawar nor Sunetra Pawar had informed him.
items.title: Maharashtra CM Defends UCC Draft Amid NCP Merger Speculation

items.summary: The release of Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, triggered a public dispute between the BJP and Congress over how it portrays Indian history. The BJP accused the book of whitewashing wrongs by the Nehru-Gandhi family, while Congress leaders countered that the ruling party was reviving old controversies ahead of Punjab elections. Opposing parties defended Gandhi's accounts, with PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti praising her as a stateswoman and Congress MP Pramod Tiwari calling the BJP's reaction a habit to benefit politically.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi memoir ignites BJP-Congress historical feud

items.summary: The Madras High Court ordered an FIR, freezing of bank accounts for Agal Vilakku Publication and proprietor Mohan, disciplinary action including suspension, and scrutiny of the amount spent on books. A Division Bench directed the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption to register the case immediately, per Press Trust of India. The court treated long-undebated allegations as unrebutted, citing repackaging of older works such as a 2013 book falsely presented as Kalki's work. It also referenced Jean Dreze denouncing another fake attribution at the Kalaignar Centenary Library in Madurai.
items.title: Madras HC Orders FIR and Account Freezes Over Fake Library Book Purchases

items.summary: In her newly released autobiography Belonging: A Journey of Love, Sonia Gandhi recounts how 10-year-old Rahul relayed the news that his uncle Sanjay Gandhi had died in a plane crash on June 23, 1980. After receiving the message from RK Dhawan—"There has been an accident, Rahul. Chacha has died," Dhawan said—the boy repeated "Chacha e morto" while relaying it to his grandmother in Italy. The account also reflects on Italian as a family language and captures Indira Gandhi's grief over her son.
items.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls Rahul relaying Sanjay's death
